body:
OBSERVED 2026-08-29 on the household production instance:

    WARN {cps.ub:4517} NETWORK_SHARE_MODE=true disables SQLite WAL for every database,
    including app.db /config/app.db even when /config is on local disk ... app.db is using
    legacy sqlite3 transaction control with a rollback journal; call sites requiring
    contained SAVEPOINTs acquire a local write transaction.

Measured configuration divergence:

| where | NETWORK_SHARE_MODE |
|---|---|
| production (teenyverse), read via `docker inspect calibre-web` | **true** - WAL disabled |
| `local-dev/docker-compose.local.yml` | false |
| `local-dev/docker-compose.dev-live.yml` | false |
| `local-dev/docker-compose.bindmount.yml` | false |
| `local-dev/private-e2e-rig.sh` | unset (=> false) |

PROVENANCE, because the four rig files are NOT in this repository and a reader
cannot check them: `local-dev/` is untracked, living beside the checkout in the
operator's private control directory (the same place `scripts/lib/pr-lifecycle.sh`
and `agent-context/` live). So those four rows are unverifiable from the repo and
nothing here will invalidate them when a rig changes. What IS checkable in-repo,
and is the load-bearing half of the finding: `NETWORK_SHARE_MODE` defaults to
false (`cps/sqlite_utils.py`), the warning text is emitted from `cps/ub.py`, and
therefore anything booting through `_create_app_db_engine` without the variable
set runs WAL - including this commit's own new test.

So every local rig, and therefore every local e2e run and every container-based verification,
exercises the opposite transaction mode from the one production actually runs. Stated precisely:
the divergence is in everything reaching app.db through `_create_app_db_engine` with the variable
unset. A test that opens app.db with raw `sqlite3` already gets production's rollback journal;
that narrower claim is the accurate one and it is sufficient.

Why this matters more than it looks: #1936 reworked app.db transaction control around
`BEGIN IMMEDIATE` and contained SAVEPOINTs, explicitly because of WAL semantics
(`SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT` under a deferred BEGIN). That work, its concurrency evidence, and
everything since built on it - including #1939's chunked membership seed, which commits in
bounded chunks specifically to avoid holding the writer slot - has been validated under WAL
and ships to a server with WAL disabled. The seed was OBSERVED committing 222 rows cleanly on the real production
config on 2026-08-29 (account id 107, teenyverse `calibre-web`; membership row count read back as
222 with zero `database is locked` in the container log). So this is not a known defect; it is an
untested axis that happens to work.

The uncomfortable part: this was discovered by accident, from a startup warning, while doing
something else. The information was one `docker inspect` away for the entire session. Nobody
had compared rig configuration to production configuration.

Fix shape, cheapest first:
1. Make the rigs able to mirror production: a NETWORK_SHARE_MODE toggle on the e2e rig and a
   compose variant with it true.
2. Better: run the concurrency-shaped suites in BOTH modes in CI, the way the E2E lane now
   pins its image - the two modes are different enough that a pass in one is not evidence for
   the other.
3. Cheapest of all and worth doing regardless: assert at startup, in a test, that the rig's
   mode is stated rather than defaulted, so a future session sees the axis exists.

Related class: FAILURE-MODES 6 (every gate boots an EMPTY database) - same shape, different
axis. Both are "the thing we test is not the thing we ship", and both were invisible until
someone ran the real artifact against the real configuration.
title: Every local rig runs NETWORK_SHARE_MODE=false; production runs true, so no local test exercises prod's transaction mode
